insights.insight: Crinkl has confirmed 93,237 cryptographically verified receipts representing $4.9M in cumulative GMV — this is deterministic purchase proof, not modeled intent, at a scale that supports statistically meaningful category and brand analysis.

Grocery-supermarkets accounts for 1,505 receipts and $66,652 in verified GMV over 14 days, nearly double the next category; Walmart leads all brands at 356 receipts, with Costco, Kroger, Aldi, and Safeway rounding out the top five — a clear signal of where verified consumer spend is concentrated.

The network is processing 326–398 verified receipts per day on a sustained basis, with a confirmed intraday pattern — morning UTC trough followed by afternoon recovery and a late-evening burst window — giving planners a predictable data refresh cadence.

insights.topic: QSR and home improvement entering verified receipt mix
insights.insight: McDonald's, Lowe's, and H-E-B have each entered the brand visibility list since October 12, extending verified purchase coverage beyond grocery into QSR and home improvement — categories where probabilistic targeting has historically struggled with purchase confirmation.

insights.topic: 17 active metro areas with category-level granularity
insights.insight: Verified spend is distributed across 30 category/metro cells in 17 active metros, enabling geographic segmentation grounded in confirmed transactions rather than device-location inference — a meaningful distinction for regional campaign planning.

insights.topic: Receipt velocity recovering after brief deceleration
insights.insight: Token acceleration dipped below 1.0x for two snapshots on October 18–19 then recovered to 1.046x–1.074x across four consecutive snapshots, confirming the slowdown was transient and that the underlying receipt intake rate remains structurally intact.
